title: Indian Shares Poised for Muted Open Amidst Oil Price Concerns and Foreign Outflows
description: Indian benchmark indices are set for a cautious start, despite positive cues from the IT sector. HCLTech's Q2 FY27 earnings surpassed expectations, reporting .

faq.q: What are FPI outflows and why do they matter?
faq.a: FPI outflows refer to foreign portfolio investors selling their investments in a country's financial markets and repatriating the money. They matter because large outflows can depress stock prices, weaken the local currency, and signal a lack of confidence in the economy.

faq.q: How do rising crude oil prices affect the Indian economy?
faq.a: Rising crude oil prices negatively impact India by increasing the import bill, widening the current account deficit, potentially depreciating the rupee, and fueling inflation through higher transportation and production costs.

faq.q: Did HCLTech's earnings truly beat expectations?
faq.a: Yes, HCLTech's Q2 FY27 net profit of ₹5,132 crore and revenue of ₹35,620 crore both surpassed analyst estimates, contributing to a positive sentiment for the IT sector.

faq.q: What is HCLTech's outlook for the rest of FY27?
faq.a: HCLTech has narrowed its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5-4% in constant currency and retained its EBIT margin guidance at 17.5-18.5%, indicating cautious optimism despite a volatile global environment.

faq.q: Is the Indian IT sector resilient to global slowdowns?
faq.a: While the Indian IT sector has shown resilience, particularly with growth in advanced AI services, it is not entirely immune to global macroeconomic slowdowns and client spending uncertainties.

faq.q: What role is AI playing in the IT sector's growth?
faq.a: AI is emerging as a significant growth driver, with companies like HCLTech reporting substantial increases in advanced AI revenue. It is also expected to create new market opportunities, though it may cause some deflation in traditional IT services.
